root_cause.mechanism: When using `import_name = "__main__"`, `importlib.util.find_spec` can raise `ValueError` (specifically `ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None`) if `__main__.__spec__` is not set or None. Calls to `importlib.util.find_spec` in `get_root_path` and `_find_package_path` were not uniformly wrapped in `try...except (ImportError, ValueError):`, leading to unhandled `ValueError` when initializing Flask as a direct script.

hypotheses.text: When import_name is '__main__', importlib.util.find_spec(root_mod_name) raises ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None (because __main__.__spec__ can be None when running a script directly without a module spec or when __spec__ isn't set yet). In _find_package_path, ValueError is caught inside try...except (ImportError, ValueError): around root_spec = importlib.util.find_spec(root_mod_name), but later in _find_package_path, spec = importlib.util.find_spec(root_mod_name) is called *outside* the try-except block at line 858!
hypotheses.predicts: Catching ValueError in addition to ImportError around importlib.util.find_spec in _find_package_path (and/or anywhere else find_spec is called with __main__ or arbitrary names) will prevent ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None and allow falling back to cwd correctly.
